document.title: Usama bin Ladin: Saudi Government Reportedly Turning the Screws on the Taliban on Visas; Haj May be Affected
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), 1998 Missile Strikes on Bin Laden May Have Backfired
document.note: [Confidential] In response to Taliban intransigence on surrendering bin Laden, Saudi Arabia is restricting Afghan travel to the holy sites and reportedly barred Ariana from flying between Kabul or Kandahar and Jeddah. The Taliban would suffer great embarrassment if the Saudi government does not accept their Haj list. Excised.

events.description: Saudi Arabia closed its Kabul embassy and downgraded ties with the Taliban over Bin Ladin.
Saudis reportedly told the Taliban to stop Ariana flights to Jeddah.
Muhammad Muslim Haqqani visited Saudi Arabia seeking Haj permission for 8,000 Afghans; left empty-handed.
Taliban envoy Syedur Rahman Haqqani told a source the Saudis refuse visas for Taliban-recommended Afghans; a Saudi official also met someone in Islamabad about a Haj list of 500.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting Saudi pressure on the Taliban over visas and Haj.
Saudi Arabia closed its embassy in Kabul and downgraded ties with the Taliban over the bin Ladin issue.
Saudi Arabia reportedly told the Taliban to stop Ariana flights to Jeddah.
Muhammad Muslim Haqqani visited Saudi Arabia, requested haj permission for 8,000 Afghans, left without a decision.
Taliban envoy Syedur Rahman Haqqani told a source that the Saudis refuse visas for Taliban-recommended Afghans.
A source met a Saudi official in Islamabad, who asked for a list of 500 Afghans for haj.
Source met the political officer and recounted Haqqani's complaints about Saudi visa refusals.
NIMA representative and others briefed the political officer on Saudi visa and Ariana flight policy.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reports Saudi pressure on Taliban via visas over bin Ladin.
Last haj period, when Saudi officials generally favored the Taliban's list over anti-Taliban referrals.
Next haj expected to take place.

key_claims: Saudi Arabia was quietly pressuring the Taliban via visa denials over their refusal to act on Bin Ladin.
Saudi Arabia was considering rejecting the Taliban's Haj list, which sought 8,000 pilgrims, linking it explicitly to Bin Ladin.
Saudi Arabia reportedly halted Ariana flights to Jeddah in October 1998.
Saudi Arabia closed its Kabul embassy in September 1998 and downgraded ties with the Taliban.
The Saudis showed a friendlier face to anti-Taliban factions such as NIMA and the Northern Alliance.
The US Embassy assessed that Taliban isolation and pressure to deal with Bin Ladin would deepen.
